title: Every 10 minutes, a quiet connection to somewhere odd
intro: The network team noticed a pattern in VPC flow logs: every 10 minutes, app-02 makes a short HTTPS connection to 91.215.85.17, an IP with no link to any vendor you use. CPU and memory look normal, and nothing seems broken. Regular, low-volume check-ins like this are called 'beaconing'.

steps.prompt: Catch it in the act: watch established connections to 91.215.85.17 on app-02, refreshing every second (watch -n1).
steps.hint: watch reruns a command at an interval.

steps.prompt: A python3 process, pid 31877. See its full command line and parent: show ps for that pid with ppid and args.
steps.fake_output:
PID  PPID USER     COMMAND
31877     1 appsvc   python3 /opt/app/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/dbus_update/helper.py

steps.prompt: Started by PID 1 (systemd), not by the app. Find the systemd timer that runs it.
steps.fake_output:
NEXT                        LEFT    UNIT                  ACTIVATES
Sun 2026-09-28 11:10:00 UTC 6min    dbus-update.timer     dbus-update.service
Sun 2026-09-28 12:00:00 UTC 56min   logrotate.timer       logrotate.service
steps.hint: list-timers shows every scheduled systemd unit.

steps.prompt: Read the unit file behind dbus-update.service.
steps.hint: systemctl cat shows a unit's files.

steps.prompt: It runs code from inside the app's Python virtualenv: a malicious package. Find which installed package it belongs to: pip show dbus-update, using the venv's pip.
steps.fake_output:
Name: dbus-update
Version: 0.3.1
Summary: D-Bus helpers
Required-by: requets
steps.hint: The venv's own pip knows what's installed in it.

steps.prompt: Required by 'requets', a typosquat of 'requests'. Contain: stop and disable the timer so it can't run again.
steps.hint: disable --now stops it and prevents it starting again.

resolution: This was a software supply-chain attack. Someone added 'requets' (one letter off 'requests') to requirements.txt. That typosquatted package pulled in a malicious dependency whose install step created a systemd timer disguised as a D-Bus helper, which checked in with a command-and-control server every 10 minutes. There were no CPU spikes and nothing broke: beaconing is quiet by design, and only network pattern analysis caught it. Remaining work: find which commit added 'requets' and whether other services use it (a lock-file search across repos); treat every credential app-02 could read as stolen and rotate it; rebuild the host; block 91.215.85.17 at the egress firewall; and check flow logs for other hosts talking to it. Prevention: pin and hash-check dependencies (pip --require-hashes, lock files), pull from an internal package proxy with an allowlist, scan dependencies in CI, and default-deny egress, so an unknown IP can't be reached at all.
